values: You would like to change your address and telephone number, correct? Whose registered details would you like to change?

First, the details for my own account. My family is moving to the same new address, so I thought that changing my details would mean all notices for accounts in their names would come to this address too.
Explain in Japanese that you thought changing your address would also redirect all notices for accounts in the names of family members moving with you to the same new address.
We cannot tell you that changes to details registered under other people's names can be completed through your own change procedure. Have you brought your own identification documents today?
I have a document showing my new address. I do not want to include my family's accounts in my application. I would like to ask separately what my family members should inquire about themselves.
Show the document with your new address. Say in Japanese that you will not include your family's accounts and would like to ask separately about inquiries they should make themselves.
We will keep your changes separate from your family's. For the telephone number change, we will also check which number we can reach you at.
This is my new number. I am not planning to enter a family member's number as my own. Please check again that both my address and telephone number are included in the changes.
Show your new telephone number. Say in Japanese that you will not use a family member's number as your own, and ask for a check that both your address and telephone number are to be changed.

We will clarify which details need changing and refer you to the staff responsible for identity checks and the application procedure. Please also confirm their explanation of when the change will be reflected in the mailing address.

I do not assume that making the request today guarantees even notices already prepared for dispatch will reach my new address. I would like to ask what can be checked about notices sent before and after the change takes effect.

Say in Japanese that requesting the change today does not guarantee that notices already prepared will go to the new address. Ask what can be checked about notices before and after the change takes effect.
The staff member will explain what can be checked. For notices addressed to your family, please ask separately what guidance your family members should receive themselves.

I will check only the changes to my own address and telephone number, and I will not tell my family that their changes are complete too. Before submitting the application, I will reread the entries and listen to the explanation of the mailing address and when the change takes effect.

Say in Japanese that you will check only your own address and telephone number changes and will not tell your family their changes are complete. Explain that before applying, you will check the entries and the explanation of where notices will be sent and when the change takes effect.
We will start by checking your own details. Neither completion of your changes nor changes to accounts in your family members' names have been confirmed yet. Please excuse me.
Would you like to ask about the information on this snack's label?
I have a nut allergy. I thought I could not see nuts in the ingredients list, but there is a statement about the same factory below it, and I have not managed to read all of it.
Say in Japanese that you have a nut allergy, cannot see nuts in the ingredients list, but have not fully read the warning about the same factory.
Let's read the ingredients list separately from this warning. The text below says that products containing nuts are manufactured in the same factory.

I will not decide that I can eat it just because I cannot see nuts listed. The warning also does not state that the product definitely contains nuts, so I cannot decide for myself that it is safe or low risk.

Say in Japanese that you will not assume the product is suitable just because nuts are absent from the list, or that the factory warning means it definitely contains nuts. Explain that you will not judge it safe or low risk yourself.
I cannot guarantee that you can eat it either. If you want to ask about anything unclear, we can check the product name and the manufacturer's contact details on the label.
I will not buy it today. I will note the product name and the warning so I can ask about them. I will not try eating a little to check.
Say in Japanese that you will not buy it today, will note the product name and warning for an inquiry, and will not test it by tasting it.
Please make a note of the label information and consider it. The storage section also gives separate instructions for before and after opening.

I would like to record the ingredients, factory warning and storage instructions separately so I do not mix them up when I ask. I will also check which storage conditions the date on the label applies to.
Say in Japanese that you want to record the ingredients, factory warning and storage instructions separately, and also read which storage conditions apply to the date on the label.
Please check this product's date together with its storage conditions. Do not decide from just part of the label that it can be kept until the same date after opening.

I will organize the label information without assuming that the conditions for an unopened product also apply after opening. After asking the manufacturer about anything unclear, I will reconsider which product meets my needs.

Say in Japanese that you will not apply unopened-product conditions after opening. Explain that you will organize the label information, ask the manufacturer about anything unclear, and then reconsider your choice.
Understood. Today you are only checking the label, without buying the product. Please use your notes when making your inquiry. Thank you.
May I ask what you would like from your walk in the park? How would you like to spend your time?
I would like a short walk and then to sit somewhere quiet. But I can hear noise from the nearby plaza, so I would also like to know about routes other than the circuit through the plaza.
Say in Japanese that you want a short walk and a quiet rest, but can hear noise from the plaza. Ask about routes other than the circuit through it.
There is an event announced for the plaza today. One option is a short walk out and back along the trees, but we cannot guarantee that you will not hear the noise there.
Rather than going a long way in search of somewhere guaranteed to be quiet, I will see what a nearby path is like. Please also tell me whether there is somewhere to sit along the way.
Say in Japanese that you will try a nearby path instead of going far to find guaranteed quiet. Ask whether there is somewhere to sit along the way.
There is a bench marked just before the path along the trees. You can check it by taking this path, rather than a shortcut across the event area.

I will not cut through the event. I will follow the route you showed me and go only as far as the bench. Before going ahead, I would like to check for steps or changes in level on site as well as on the map.
Say in Japanese that you will avoid crossing the event area and go only as far as the bench by the trees. Explain that you want to check for changes in level on site before proceeding.
Please check the signs and the path surface when you get there. If you cannot use the bench, another option is to return toward the entrance.

If I cannot sit down, I will not keep walking a long way looking for another seat. I would like to return if the noise or tiredness bothers me, so please mark a landmark on the paper to help me get back to this entrance.

Say in Japanese that you will not keep walking a long way looking for another seat if none is available. Ask for a landmark on paper to help you return to this entrance if noise or fatigue bothers you.
I have marked the information board near the entrance as a landmark. Please check the signs for the way back so you do not accidentally leave through a different exit for the event.

I will take a short walk out and back, returning to the information board. If the seating or noise level does not suit me, I will not extend the walk. I will return to the entrance and may end today's walk there.

Say in Japanese that you will take a short walk out and back to the information board. Explain that if the seating or quiet is unsuitable, you will return to the entrance without extending the walk and consider ending it for today.
Please take this paper with you. Avoid the event area and adjust your plans to how you feel and the conditions around you. Enjoy your walk.
That is a large piece of luggage. Do you have something showing which service you are taking?
I am taking the bus shown on this reservation slip. My suitcase is heavy, so please tell me how to get there without using stairs.
Show the service on your reservation slip and ask in Japanese for a route avoiding stairs because your suitcase is heavy.
That service departs from bay four on the second floor. You can use the elevator on the right, but there is a short queue at the moment.
There are twenty minutes until departure. Do you think I can reach the bay in time, including the wait for the elevator?
Say in Japanese that departure is in twenty minutes and ask whether you can reach the bay in time, including the elevator wait.
The journey usually takes about five minutes, but we cannot predict the waiting time. You can tell the attendant at the queue what time your bus departs.
I will speak to the attendant first. Is there somewhere I can wait with my luggage beside me?
Say in Japanese that you will tell the attendant your departure time, and ask for a waiting place where you can put your luggage beside you.
There is a waiting area beside the entrance to the queue. Do you have family with you? It is easier to guide you if you queue together.
My mother is sitting on that chair. She also walks slowly, so the two of us will move to the waiting area together.
Say in Japanese that your mother is sitting on the chair and walks slowly, and explain that you will both move to the waiting area.
There are two of you, then. If you need assistance getting to the bay, please ask the attendant. I will also explain your situation to them.
I can carry the luggage myself, but I would like someone to guide us to the bay at my mother's walking pace.
Say in Japanese that you can carry the luggage yourself, but ask to be guided to the bay at your mother's walking pace.
I will pass that request on to the attendant. First, please wait with your mother in the waiting area. Have a safe journey.
You would like advice about registering your move here, correct? Have you brought anything with your new address written on it?
I brought my rental agreement, but the room-number field is blank. What should I write on the application form?
Say in Japanese that the rental agreement has no room number, and ask what to write on the application form.
Let's confirm the correct number instead of filling it in by guesswork. Can you contact your landlord or someone who knows?
I can call the landlord now. I would like to check how the address should be written as well, before I fill it in.
Say in Japanese that you can call the landlord now and will check how to write the address before filling in the form.
Let's leave this field blank until it is confirmed. Could you show me the other documents you have brought?
These are the document I received from my previous municipality and my residence card. I also have an envelope my company gave me, but I do not know whether I am allowed to open it.
Show the two documents you have brought. Say in Japanese that you do not know whether you may open the envelope from your company.
Please do not open the envelope without checking. Ask your company where it is to be submitted and what it contains. Are you the only person moving this time?
Yes, just me. I am enrolled in my company's insurance, so I would also like to check whether I need any separate insurance procedures.
Say in Japanese that you are moving alone and are enrolled in your company's insurance, and that you want to check whether separate insurance procedures are required.
We will refer your insurance inquiry to the specialist counter. Could you first confirm the address and then come back here?
I will finish the call to my landlord and return to this counter. Could you also write down where I should ask about insurance?
Say in Japanese that you will return to the same counter after calling your landlord, and ask for the insurance inquiry contact in writing.
I will write the contact here. Please keep the envelope as it is while you are checking about it. Please excuse me for now.
I understand you are having trouble with an appointment. If you are happy to speak to me as a nurse, I can first listen to your situation.
I have an appointment at nine next Tuesday, but my work schedule has changed and I cannot attend. I would like to ask about moving it to the afternoon.
Say in Japanese that your appointment is at nine next Tuesday and your work schedule has changed. Ask about changing it to the afternoon.
Reception handles appointment changes. Has there been any change in how you are feeling?
There has been no particular change since my last consultation. But I cannot judge for myself whether it is all right to delay the appointment.
Say in Japanese that your condition has not changed, but you cannot decide for yourself whether postponing the consultation is appropriate.
We will need to check that with the doctor. I will look at your appointment slip and put you in touch with the department responsible for your care.
Here is my appointment slip. I could take time off work on Thursday of the same week. Could you pass on that preference too?
Show your appointment slip and ask in Japanese for your availability on Thursday of the same week to be passed on.
I will tell them you would prefer Thursday. I cannot confirm a new date and time here, but reception can check for available appointments.
Then I would like to keep my Tuesday appointment for now and decide after hearing about Thursday's availability and the doctor's answer.
Ask in Japanese for the original appointment to be kept until you hear about availability on Thursday and the doctor's answer.
I will also pass on your request not to cancel the original appointment first. Reception is at the consultation counter on the right. How should I write your name on the referral slip?
Please use Nguyen An, as on my appointment slip. I will take this referral slip and my appointment slip to the counter on the right.
Ask in Japanese for the referral slip to use the same name as your appointment slip. Say you will take both slips to reception on the right.
Nguyen An, understood. I have written your requests on the referral slip I am giving you. Please discuss them with reception. Take care.
You said your bicycle is missing. Please tell me when you last saw it and when you noticed it was gone.
I left it in the bicycle parking area behind the store at eight last night. When I returned at seven this morning, it was not there. I may have mixed up the location.
Describe in Japanese the situation at eight last night and seven this morning, and explain that you may have confused the location.
So you do not yet know what happened in between. Have you checked with the manager of the bicycle parking area?
The store is not open yet, so I have not been able to check. I will also look again to see whether there was a notice at the entrance saying where bicycles had been moved.
Say in Japanese that you have not checked with the manager because the store is not open, and that you will look again for a notice about where bicycles were moved.
We will keep what you have confirmed separate from what is still unknown. What color is the bicycle, and does it have any identifying features?
It is silver, with a blue string tied to the rear basket. I have a photograph of the bicycle and a copy of its anti-theft registration.
Describe the silver bicycle and blue string in Japanese, and say that you have a photograph and a copy of the anti-theft registration.
Please show me the photograph and registration copy. What was the state of the locks when you last saw it?
I remember locking the rear wheel, but I cannot remember whether I used the separate cable lock.
Say in Japanese that you remember locking the rear wheel, but are unsure whether you used the cable lock.
You can leave the parts you do not remember as uncertain. Could you let us know the result after checking with the store?
I will ask the manager whether it was moved and let you know the result. I would like to note this office's contact details so I can do that.
Say in Japanese that you will report the result of checking with the manager, and ask for this office's contact details.
I will give you a sheet with the contact details. After hearing what you find out, we will explain any reports you need to make. Take care on your way home.
Before we accept the item, please tell me the destination and how you would like to send it.
I am sending documents to this organization for an application. I would like a method that lets me check for myself afterward whether they have arrived.
Show where you are sending the application documents, and ask in Japanese for a method that lets you check their delivery status yourself.
We can explain methods with tracking. Has the organization receiving the documents specified a shipping method?
The instructions say to keep a record of dispatch. Does that mean I need the recipient's stamp as well?
Read the instruction to keep a record of dispatch and ask in Japanese whether a recipient's stamp is also required.
That wording alone does not tell us whether a recipient's stamp is required. A record that the item was accepted for posting and confirmation from the recipient are separate matters.
I do not want to confuse the required records, so I will check with the organization receiving the documents. Until then, may I take the envelope home without leaving it here?
Say in Japanese that you will check the requirements with the recipient, and ask whether you may take the unsent envelope home.
We have not accepted it yet, so you may take it home. Is there anything about how to write the address that concerns you?
I have written the department name, but I do not know the contact person's name. Could you compare it with the address in the instructions and check whether anything is missing?
Say in Japanese that you have written the department name but do not know the contact person's name. Ask for it to be checked against the instructions.
You have included the department name as the instructions specify. It would also be a good idea to ask the recipient whether a contact person's name is additionally required.
I will come back to send it after checking the shipping method and whether a contact person's name is needed. The originals are inside, but I will first make copies to keep myself as well.
Say in Japanese that you will return after checking the shipping method and need for a contact person's name, and that you will also make copies of the originals for your own records.
I will return your envelope and the instructions. Please tell us your required conditions after checking. Take care on your way home.
You would like to ask about opening an account in advance, correct? What kinds of transactions do you mainly plan to use it for?
It is for receiving my salary from the company I start working for this month. This bank's name was on the company's form, so I came to ask about it.
Explain in Japanese that the account is for receiving your salary and that you came because the company's form named this bank.
We need to check whether that is a requirement or just an example. Do you have that form and something that confirms your name?
I have the form and my residence card. My name is shortened partway through on the company's form, but it is written in full on my card.
Show the company form and residence card. Explain in Japanese the difference between the shortened name and the full official spelling.
Please do not copy the shortened name straight onto the application form. Let's first check the full official spelling. Can you also ask your company about the name on its form?
I can check with the person responsible. I will ask both whether I must use an account at this bank and how to correct my name.
Say in Japanese that you will ask the person responsible two things: whether this bank is required and how to correct your name.
After you have checked, we will explain how to apply. Has your employer given you a deadline for submitting an account number?
They said by Friday. But I would like to tell my company that I may not be able to open the account here today.
Say in Japanese that the deadline for submitting your account number is Friday and that you want to tell your company same-day account opening is not guaranteed.
Yes. Because we need to check documents and conduct a review, we cannot promise that an account will be opened or give a completion date. Would you like to make a note of today's discussion?
I will note that I need to ask my company whether this bank is required and how to correct my name, then come back to discuss it with their answer. I will not submit the application form yet.
Say in Japanese that you will note the steps for returning with your company's answer and will hold off submitting the application form.
We will proceed in that order. Once your company has replied, please come back to the counter to discuss it. Thank you for coming today.
Are you asking about a product on that shelf? Could you tell me which size you are looking for?
I am looking for the six-hundred-milliliter detergent. Is this bag above the 298-yen price label the right one?
Say in Japanese that you want 600 mL, point out the 298-yen label, and ask whether it corresponds to the bag you are holding.
That label is for 600 mL, but the bag you are holding is 900 mL. This smaller bag is the 600 mL size.
I will take the smaller one. Does this two-for-500-yen offer apply only if I buy two with the same scent?
Choose the 600 mL bag and ask in Japanese whether the two-for-500-yen offer requires both to have the same scent.
According to this label, you can combine different scents of the 600 mL products in the same series. The 900 mL size is excluded, and you do not need to register as a member.
So if I buy one unscented bag and one floral-scented bag, the total is 500 yen including tax even if I am not a member, correct?
Confirm in Japanese that one bag of each of two scents costs a total of 500 yen including tax for a nonmember.
Yes, the displayed price includes tax. However, both of these are refill pouches. Do you have the original bottle designed for this product?
I have just moved and do not have the original bottle. I will not take the two refill pouches; I would like one original bottle with a pump instead.
Say in Japanese that you do not have the original bottle and want to change from two refill pouches to one original bottle with a pump.
The original bottles are here and cost 380 yen including tax. They are not included in the two-item discount mentioned earlier. Which scent would you like?
I will buy one unscented original bottle for 380 yen. Since I am not buying the two pouches, please tell me where to put them back on the shelf.
Choose one unscented original bottle for 380 yen and ask in Japanese where to return the pouches you are not buying.
I will put the pouches back for you. Please take this bottle to the checkout. We look forward to your next visit.
reason: Restore full natural conversational clauses and complete task hints, correcting meaning, scope, register, and formatting defects after Japanese scenario-context review.
